sections.label: Parliamentary questions on school bullying
sections.summary: Questions ask the Education Minister about anti-bullying frameworks, disciplinary measures, victim and perpetrator follow-up, teacher investigation timelines, and the Sengkang Green Primary School incident.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education whether the Ministry will consider (a) reviewing existing anti-bullying disciplinary and rehabilitation frameworks to render them more robust; (b) augmenting suspension-based punitive measures with in-school structured reflection, supervised work and restorative conferences, instead of home suspensions; (c) setting minimum competencies and staff-training hours to strengthen educators' capabilities to handle bullying; and (d) pilot cluster-level bullying support teams by counsellors/para-counsellors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what is the framework for determining the extent of disciplinary measures to be taken against perpetrators of bullying incidents that have been reported in primary schools and secondary schools; (b) what are the follow-up measures that are taken to address the needs of victims and perpetrators; and (c) what is the Ministry’s assessment of the effectiveness of the measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) how quickly are teachers expected to investigate and take action after a report of bullying has been made; and (b) whether the Ministry’s protocols on bullying are followed throughout the process in the recent bullying incident at Sengkang Green Primary School.

sections.label: Bullying investigation timelines and student separation
sections.summary: Questions ask about established timelines for schools to investigate bullying and update parents, and measures to separate involved students during investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Education (a) what are the established timelines for schools to investigate bullying incidents and to provide updates to the parents of involved students; and (b) what specific measures are implemented to separate the involved students during an investigation to ensure the victim's safety on school premises and prevent fear-based absenteeism or the need for a school transfer.

sections.label: MOE stance against hurtful behaviours
sections.summary: The Ministry of Education states it takes a firm stance against all forms of hurtful behaviours, from insensitive comments to bullying and physical violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, the Ministry of Education (MOE) takes a firm stance against all forms of hurtful behaviours, from once-off, insensitive comments to persistent intentional acts of bullying and physical violence.

sections.label: 2020 Character and Citizenship Education review
sections.summary: In 2020 MOE reviewed the Character and Citizenship Education curriculum, also examining bullying, leading to CCE-related enhancements implemented in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2020, MOE conducted a review on the Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In the context of that larger review, MOE also looked at the issue of bullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This led to a number of CCE-related enhancements, which were implemented in 2021.

sections.label: Peer support system in schools
sections.summary: Schools established a peer support system where students are taught to support one another, be upstanders, and look out for peers lacking strong friend support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Second, schools established a peer support system in every school, where students are taught how to support one another, be an upstander and look out for those who do not have strong support from their friends in school.

sections.label: Tiered school disciplinary measures
sections.summary: Schools use a tiered approach to discipline based on severity, ranging from reflection and detention to suspension and caning, with Police reports for severe bullying.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They adopt a tiered approach for disciplinary measures based on the severity of the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Such measures range from reflection for careless remarks to detention or suspension for more serious cases, and caning for boys in egregious cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For severe bullying that warrants Police attention, a Police report will be made and perpetrators may face legal consequences.

sections.label: MOE bullying review since 2025
sections.summary: MOE has been conducting a comprehensive review of bullying since early 2025, shared at an August 27 dialogue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As I shared on 27 August this year at a dialogue with educators, parents and community partners, MOE had been conducting a comprehensive review of bullying since early 2025.

sections.label: Suggestions for schools and parents
sections.summary: Suggestions include more school resources, parent support groups, parent updates on CCE lessons and peer upstander education, with recommendations due in the first half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: These include providing schools with more resources to investigate and deal with cases, involving parents support groups to support parents whose children are involved in bullying, keeping parents informed about the content of CCE lessons so that they can reinforce values education at home and involving peers to educate others on being an upstander – among many other suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will consider all these suggestions as well as ideas raised by Members seriously, before finalising the recommendations which we aim to release in the first half of 2026.

sections.label: Children learn from environments
sections.summary: Children model behaviours and pick up values from home, school and community, with over 400,000 children in primary and secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In this, children model behaviours and pick up values from the home environment, their school environment and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have some 400,000 over children in our primary and secondary schools, and their daily interactions in class, outside class, outside school.

sections.label: Calm correction and disciplinary consequences
sections.summary: Some children may have special needs or other issues, and learn best through calm correction, reflection, amends, disciplinary consequences and being welcomed back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And some of it could be a function of their conditions – some may have special needs or other issues that they are grappling with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They learn best through calm correction from adults, reflecting on how they should have behaved, make amends for their behaviour, experience disciplinary consequences and being welcomed back to their social circles with continued guidance and support.

sections.label: Parent toolkit accessibility and educator stance
sections.summary: A Member asks how the toolkit can be used further to support parents of bullies and victims, and seeks assurance for educators to take a harder stance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In fact, I have questioned before, how accessible it is for our parents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: So, my question is, how do we make use of this toolkit further to prevent and empower parents to help them in their journey in helping their children when they are bullied or, in this case, both sides, whether it is the perpetrator or the victim, I think we need to give the right support for them.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Is there some assurance from the Ministry, so that our educators can take a harder stance sometimes and balance it, as we approach our students moving forward?

sections.label: Tiered tools for educators
sections.summary: Schools have a suite of tools for a tiered approach, from reflection and learning for mild cases to suspension and detention for severe cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of educators, we have, as I said, a suite of tools that schools can use as a tiered approach, from reflection and learning for mild cases or careless cases or hurtful comments, to more severe punitive measures, such as suspension, detention.

sections.label: Purpose of disciplinary measures
sections.summary: Disciplinary measures aim to teach children that behaviours have consequences, suit the context and children, and encourage learning, reflection and restored relationships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: But all in, when I describe the multi-tiered approach in terms of the severity, if I may use that word loosely, of disciplinary measures, I think we must keep emphasising the fact that these are intended to help the child understand that there are consequences for certain behaviours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Those disciplinary measures must be appropriate to the context and to the children involved, as well as conduce to learn from their mistakes, reflection, restoration of relationships, including mutual apologies or apologies of the appropriate kind and then the children move forward.

sections.label: In-house suspension proposal
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE could consider moving from home suspension to in-house suspension in school.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could MOE consider moving from home suspension to in-house suspension in school?

sections.label: Anti-retaliation clause request
sections.summary: The passage asks MOE to consider a standard anti-retaliation clause, explicit consequences for post-report harassment, and communicating this to students and parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Could MOE consider a standard anti-retaliation clause, explicit consequences for post-report harassment and communicate this to students and parents, because what they do know is that for students who report, they are worried that the parents of the person that they reported on will come after them.

sections.label: In-school suspension explained
sections.summary: Schools use in-school suspension, where students are away from class but learn or do community work or service in school as a disciplinary measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For some others, it might not quite have the intended effect because they see it through a different lens and they would not mind being away from school and being at home, and worse, if there is little or no supervision at home, if parents are busy at work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Therefore, our schools also do what you call in-school suspension, where you are away from the class, but you do your learning or do some other community work or service in the school as a disciplinary measure for the actions.

sections.label: Gaps and recommendations timeline
sections.summary: The passage lists areas being looked at and states hope to roll out a suite of recommendations by the first half of next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In terms of the gaps or the possible areas that we are looking at, I have articulated them in my response: strengthening school culture, environment and processes, greater emphasis to values education, more support for schools and educators, deepening their capacity and enhancing school home partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I mentioned that we hope, by the first half of next year, to be able to roll out a suite of recommendations.

sections.label: Difficulty giving average time
sections.summary: The passage says giving an average time is hard because it depends on the facts, circumstances and severity of the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: On the second question, the Member is asking for average time, I think, that is very hard to give a clear answer to, because it really depends on the facts of the case, depends on the circumstances and depends on the severity.

sections.label: Schools look at underlying causes
sections.summary: Schools look into behaviour and principally the underlying cause when things arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In our schools, when things arise, they will look into not just the behaviour, but we principally want to look at what is the underlying cause.

sections.label: Family violence affecting school behaviour
sections.summary: Asks whether family violence at home leads children to manifest behaviour in school in a particular way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Do they come from families, as Member Elysa Chen mentioned, where there might be family violence at home and the children then manifest their behaviour in school in a particular way?

sections.label: Consistency and accountability in bullying
sections.summary: Asks how MOE ensures consistency and accountability of all parties across institutions given school autonomy in managing bullying.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: One, while I understand, this is a very complex environment in terms of bullying, there is a whole spectrum of it and we do want to give the schools autonomy in terms of managing that because two cases are never the same.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But how would MOE ensure that there is some consistency and accountability of all parties, whether it is victim, bully, family or even the educators across institutions, whether there is some consistency, because the Minister talked about best practices.

sections.label: Guidelines and cyberbullying takedown powers
sections.summary: Material is put out for parents, community and schools, and IMDA has legislation that may give powers to require takedowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Well, I mentioned earlier that there is some material that is put out for parents, for the community and, then, internally for the school community, guidelines and even some case studies on how to identify, deal with cyberbullying incidents involving children in schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I understand that the Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore has legislation that might give them powers to require takedowns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: That is, of course, asking the platform to do so if there is a threshold met.

sections.label: School leaders and restorative practice experts
sections.summary: School leaders and sometimes the Police or superintendents may be involved, and a suggestion was made to bring in restorative practice experts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: School leaders may be involved and sometimes, even beyond the school if a matter is more serious, including the Police or the superintendent, zonal directors or even headquarters itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There was a suggestion, as part of the review that is ongoing, that we bring in experts with knowledge in restorative practice, or RP, for instance.

sections.label: Safeguards against over-reporting false positives
sections.summary: Asks what safeguards prevent over-reporting of false positives that may overwhelm teachers and dilute attention from serious cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share what safeguards are in place to prevent over-reporting of false positives that may overwhelm teachers and dilute attention from serious cases?

sections.label: Bullying cover-ups and CCE evaluation
sections.summary: Member asks about cover-up reasons, penalties for schools, and how MOE evaluates CCE effectiveness given steady bullying numbers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
sentences.text: A second question would be, if no, are there any reasons to believe why cover-ups could happen?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I am not aware that there are such penalties for schools or educators if a bullying incident happens in their class or in the school.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I cannot believe there is, though I would certainly go back and check.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: When the Member mentions cover-ups, I think it is best to look at specific cases that we can then examine and investigate, if necessary, because it is a serious allegation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am very heartened to hear about the enhancements that have been made to the CCE since 2021 and I would like to ask if the Minister could elaborate on how the Ministry actually evaluates the effectiveness of some of these changes made, especially in light of some MOE statistics, as of 2024, which indicates that bullying numbers have been held steady in the last five years.

sections.label: Review of public suggestions
sections.summary: Minister says both suggestions will be studied in the review and welcomes the public to alert authorities to such sites.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The short answer to both is, we will study in the course of the review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For the Member's suggestions, on the first, we will also welcome members of the public, including Members of this House, if you have seen any of these sites, to also alert us, I think that will be the "all hands on deck" approach to looking after our children.

sections.label: Positive school culture review
sections.summary: Review aims to strengthen efforts so students speak up against unacceptable behaviour rather than stand aside.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Upstanding behaviour is not just something that our peer support leaders are trained to do.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We hope our students, as a whole, will not just stand at the side, be an audience, or worse, even implicitly egg people on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, this is really about fomenting and formulating a positive school culture and class culture, which I mentioned earlier, that is the aim of this review, to see how we can further strengthen existing efforts to create a positive school culture, not just a kind and caring culture, but one in which people speak up and make clear what is not acceptable behaviour in their midst.
